operational_constraints: Existing ambiguous duplicate push tokens lose all owners; all legacy registrations become inactive. Fresh Settings registration and an explicit category preference save are required.
Opt-out keeps an ordered inactive token tombstone. Do not purge tombstones while old registration requests or restored clients may replay.
Push dispatch is at-most-once per trip/search. A crash after claiming can omit a push; an ambiguous Expo response is not resent. An accepted ticket is not device-delivery proof.
A push already accepted by Expo cannot be recalled. Bodies omit destinations and itinerary details. Saved trip and in-app notification remain authoritative.

Deletion retains a private minimal receipt after Auth removal to recover a lost final response. Apple tokens are encrypted until revocation is accepted, then removed; Apple subject cleared on completion. Approve receipt retention/purge policy (recommended completed receipts 30 days) before launch.
A lost code exchange response before encrypted token persistence needs fresh Apple reauthentication. A changed linked Apple identity fails closed for resolution.
The native recovery proof is stored only in SecureStore. Reauthentication never opts into push; pending cleanup for another account is never transferred.

The SQL file is intentionally outside the frozen bootstrap migration inventory. Supabase CLI was unavailable and npm resolution failed; promote through an available CLI migration-new command only after review, preserving the reviewed SQL content.

Core account writes and deletion claims use transaction-scoped account advisory locks at READ COMMITTED; other isolation levels fail closed. Owned searches cannot transfer or detach. Purge removes trips before owned searches to avoid fenced foreign-key updates.

Up to 32 status-only device proofs remain valid independently for 30 days from issuance. New proofs do not evict unexpired ones; the cap rejects new issuance and permits reuse. Receipt retention must preserve all unexpired proofs.
Ordered push revocation remains active when registration/delivery flags are off. Missing ordering schema returns a retryable failure; no physical-delete fallback may erase tombstones.
device_release_checks: Native saved-trip browser handoff while signed in/out, interrupted navigation and provider final-price/terms consent.
Apple deletion: missing configuration, wrong identity, Hide My Email, linked accounts, cancel, consumed code, timeout, app restart, lost deletion response and signing in after deletion.

Push: clean install, deny/retry, OS Settings revocation, expired session reauthentication, different-account sign-in, offline opt-out, clock regression, late POST after DELETE, restored app and token rotation.
Current web/native AI consent: decline, missing/stale metadata, account switch, offline retry, saved draft after definite generation refusal, and ambiguous timeout reconnect only.
